analysis:
In the Union Budget presented on 5 July 2019, the Finance Minister announced 'Har Ghar Jal' under the Jal Jeevan Mission, with the aim of providing tap water to all rural households by 2024. The mission was subsequently launched and its period was later extended (Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, aimed at full coverage by 2028).

At the start of the mission only about 3.23 crore rural households (16.7 per cent) had tap water connections. PIB releases state that around 12.30 crore additional households had been covered by 17 March 2025, and that by 22 October 2025 over 81 per cent of rural households (more than 15.72 crore homes) had tap water. That is short of universal coverage by the 2024 deadline.

A Comptroller and Auditor General audit of implementation in Gujarat, reported in September 2026, found most tested water samples in surveyed villages unfit for consumption and flagged project delays and financial irregularities.
